name: Philippines
headline: Philippines: +4.4% growth in 2025, 1.7% inflation, debt 59% of GDP
sections: Philippines is a $487 billion economy (2025), the world's 34th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.4% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $13K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 15.3% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 1.7% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 7.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 59% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 52% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −3.3% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 67% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.7% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 56% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 69.9 years (2024). Population: 113.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
